QC report: CSF proteome (PXD016278)

Runs excluded by the authors (13) are not shown; 197 runs and 1542 protein groups remain. 385 protein groups are quantified in every run.

Run-level summary

Proteins quantified per run

Missing values bias the median of observed intensities

Spectronaut’s Local Normalization was applied across all runs. A per-run median computed on observed values alone is inflated in runs with more missing values, because missing values concentrate in low-abundance proteins.

Correlation between missing fraction and median: 0.85 using observed values, -0.12 using only the 385 complete protein groups.

Batch offset after removing the missingness effect

Normalization assessment

Per-run medians of complete protein groups were modelled on batch and diagnosis. Batch offsets are modelled as a covariate in limma rather than removed by renormalization, because run-level centering would also remove the small diagnosis-associated shift shown below.

Drivers of missingness

Missingness depends on diagnosis after adjusting for batch and age, so missing values are not independent of the contrast of interest. This rules out both left-censored imputation and analysis of observed values only, and motivates a model of the missingness mechanism in the differential abundance step.

Runs with low protein coverage

Runs more than 3 median absolute deviations below their batch median in protein groups quantified. All are retained; sample-level quality weights are estimated in the limma model.

Blood contamination

Erythrocyte contamination is scored with a panel of erythrocyte-specific proteins (Geyer et al., 2019, EMBO Mol Med). Each protein is z-scored across runs, and the run score is the mean z-score of the panel proteins it contains.

Panel protein groups found: 9 (CA1, CA2, HBD, SLC4A1, CAT, BLVRB, PRDX2, HBB, HBA1).

Contamination does not differ between diagnostic groups, so it is not expected to bias the AD vs. control comparison. 4 runs exceed the contamination threshold (median + 3 MAD = 1.37): all are retained in the main analysis and removed in a sensitivity analysis. Protein groups strongly correlated with the score are flagged as contamination-prone in the differential abundance results.

Principal component analysis

PCA on the 385 protein groups quantified in every run (no imputation), each scaled to unit variance.

PC1: brain-derived vs plasma-derived proteins

One end of PC1 is formed by neuronal and neural extracellular-matrix proteins (neurexins, NRCAM, NCAN), the other by liver- and immune-derived plasma proteins (apolipoproteins, complement, protease inhibitors). PC1 therefore reflects the balance between brain-derived and plasma-derived protein in CSF, which depends largely on blood–CSF barrier permeability. PC1 is correlated with the overall intensity level of each run (r = -0.64) and partly associated with diagnosis.

A plasma-protein score is computed as for the erythrocyte score, from 13 protein groups of classic plasma proteins (SERPINA1, GC, HP, F2, PLG, APOA1, AHSG, ALB, TF, HPX). Its correlation with PC1 is 0.88; its correlation with the erythrocyte score is -0.11.

The most distant runs lie at the plasma-rich end of PC1 and have normal erythrocyte scores: they reflect plasma protein entering CSF, not blood contamination at puncture. They are retained, since excluding them would bias the cohort towards individuals with an intact barrier. PC1 is not used as a covariate, because it carries part of the disease signal. The plasma score is used in a sensitivity analysis: candidate biomarkers that lose their association with diagnosis after adjusting for it are reported as possibly reflecting barrier permeability.
